item.description: Background: Suboptimal design of infusion pumps may lead to usage errors, thereby compromising patient safety. Nevertheless, existing research on infusion pump usability continues to exhibit limitations in aspects such as task design. item.title: AI-Enhanced Conversational Agents for Personalized Asthma Support in People With Asthma: Factors for Engagement, Value, and Efficacy in a Cross-Sectional Survey Study
item.description: Background: Asthma-related deaths in the United Kingdom are the highest in Europe, and only 30% of patients access basic care. There is a need for alternative approaches to reaching people with asthma to provide health education, self-management support, and better bridges to care. item.title: Patients’ and Health Care Professionals’ Experiences of a Digital Self-Management System for Asthma: Qualitative Study
item.description: Background: Living with asthma—especially in its severe forms—can significantly impact daily life, including social activities, work, travel, and household responsibilities. Collaboration between patients and health care professionals (HCPs) is frequently lacking, particularly regarding treatment goals. Self-management has been shown to mitigate the negative effects of asthma. Technical solutions might support self-management for patients with chronic diseases and their collaboration with HCPs.
